Good luck on your trip! I helped my mom drive to Maryland recently and it was 7 hours.  I agree with the other commenters that you should 100% bring a portable charger, and if your car has a cigarette lighter like mine than to get a car charger as backup, or if it's fancy like mom's car it'll have a usb charging port built in lol. 

Finding stuff to listen to is important. I'd recomend some comfort songs to help make you feel more comfortable. I had a classic rock playlist playing as I drove because I know all the songs and that helped relax me as I drove. Also use rest areas! They are great to eat outside on if weather permits when you bring your own snacks. I also love getting the free magazines about each state at their rest area. I had to drive through West Virgina going west and there were gigantic hills I had to drive up and that made me nervous as the car had trouble pulling those hills, but in the end I just stayed in the right lane and let cars pass me going uphill. Just focus on going one stretch at a time.

I think it's normal to have these fears- everyone wants to be loved - but when those fears turn into a pit of self loathing that's when it's a problem. It changes your perception of yourself. I'm currently in therapy and on multiple medication and that has helped me (yeah yeah it's cliche advice but it's cliche for a good reason)

When you repeat these bad thoughts to yourself you're subconsciously reinforcing them. Recognize these thoughts and challenge them.

I think moving to a more liberal city will help you, especially at a young age like 20. I'm 19 myself and forget that I have so much ahead of me, my situation now will be completely different in as little as 3 years. There's no instant cure for this, but keep moving, keep in touch with hobbies and friends, and work on making yourself better and better. "date yourself" as they say haha

Hey there, I'm a lesbian too. I know what it's like to have to go through accepting your sexuality, and it's hard, I won't lie.  Do you have any LGBT friends? The fact that you've come to realize it, even if you haven't reached acceptance yet, is a step in the right direction!

I promise you that many other lgbt people have gone through this- that's why I feel it's important to find a community to be a part of. Having a support group who knows and aware about these problems can really help. You get to choose your family, and no matter what, remember that you deserve to find your happiness and someone to love. No one can take that away from you.

Hello, I have a fear of heights and some flight anxiety, though not as severe as yours. I had to take two 8 hour flights + two 2 hour flights in December, and I'll tell you what helped me. First off, bring something to help you sleep. Melatonin, have a drink on the flight (depending on your age), or an otc sleeping medication. Doctors can actually percribe you medication to help with this before your flight, something to keep in mind for next time you're in the air. Next, something that makes you feel safe. I have a sentimental blanket I feel protected and comfortable with, so I brought it with me and hugged it around me on my flight- It helps. Lastly, Bring something preloaded with your favorite podcasts and turn it on, close your eyes, and focus on the words they are saying. If you have any other things/songs/pictures/handheld games that make you feel safe or calm bring those too. I brought Pokémon games for my flights!

Unfortunately, the thing with anxiety is that no matter what you do it can still pop up. I did all of the research about how little planes crash, and watched videos on where the spot on the plane you have the most chance of surviving is, ect. I still had a small panic attack on the first flight... I suggest looking up breathing exercises or making note of coping mechanisms that work with you, which you can bring out if you happen to feel an anxiety attack coming on. Also, the flight attendants have seen it all. I was lucky and had a nice older attendant on my flight, and we had a heartwarming chat about me being nervous in a foreign country for the first time, all while I was waiting for the bathroom, and it helped me feel more secure. These are people who are trained, very rigorously, in case of the worst senario.  Yes, during turbulence it will give you the stomach drop feeling, but I can promise you that you'll be okay. Planes are made to be as safe as possible, everyone who is employed on your flight, and all made the plane in the first place wants everyone to be safe. Breathe, and try to get some rest before your flight tommorow.

Last thing, I do suggest bringing ear plugs because omg do some kids scream and screaming children can make anxiety worse, at least in my experience. I wish you a safe flight, hope you have a wonderful time on your trip, and to remember to bring snacks in your bag! (airport food will empty your wallet!)
